## Share the conflict predicate, not the activator
sharpens-framing
Evidence: `git rev-parse HEAD` is cae371d0161bb7c03df0ab9fc312c477f7c524cc. `git show` of `packages/core/src/xbrief/verify.ts`: `verifyXbrief` checks schema, size, markdown sections, and json/md id equality. It never reads `x-directive/plan-id`. `VERIFY_USAGE` states that verify is not a lifecycle move. `git show` of `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts`: `scope:promote` and `scope:activate` call `evaluateIssuePlanIdAdmission` at the end of `runTransition`. A promote whose file is already in the target folder returns ok before that call. `git show` of `packages/core/src/vbrief-activate/activate.ts` calls the same function. In `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts` the disagree string is private `bindingIdentityConflict` (`plan.id` versus `binding.id`). The public function also mints a missing id for an ingest owner via `attachPlanIdMint` (fallback form, no REST issue id) and scans siblings with `findParentsByPlanId`. Ingest-owner detection is `/ingested from/i` on Origin or description.
Failure mode: Binding "the same identity check" as a call to `evaluateIssuePlanIdAdmission` makes `xbrief:verify` walk the lifecycle tree and mint in memory. A schema-valid brief whose `plan.id` is already taken by a sibling starts failing verify. An ingest owner with no `plan.id` is minted only in that discarded object, and verify still prints OK. The stored-mint disagree case is the part that matches the target, and it does not need the mint or the sibling scan.
Disposition: Before bind, define the shared check as the read-only stored-mint conflict: `plan.id` against the parsed `x-directive/plan-id` binding, including the other `bindingIdentityConflict` clauses. Keep `evaluateIssuePlanIdAdmission` on promote and activate. Do not call it from verify, and do not persist a mint from verify.

## The repair helper refuses the case the hint names
sharpens-framing
Evidence: `PLAN_ID_REPAIR_HINT` tells the operator to call `repairNonterminalIssuePlanIds({ vbriefDir, dryRun: true })` and then `dryRun: false`. `admissionFail` appends that hint to every identity refusal, including the disagree case. The repair skips a file `resolveIngestProvenanceOwner` classifies as not-ingest-owner. On a disagreeing binding it records action refuse and, when any row refuses, returns without writing. `git grep` at this SHA finds no use of `repairNonterminalIssuePlanIds` under `packages/cli`, `content/commands.md`, or `packages/core/src/scope/main.ts`. `attachPlanIdMint` is the only production assignment of `plan.id`, and it writes `plan.id` and the binding id as the same value. The REST form `github.issue.<numeric>` is written in `buildIssueVbrief` when `issue.id` is present. Repair's mint does not pass `issueId`.
Failure mode: A deft command that wraps `repairNonterminalIssuePlanIds` meets "names a runnable deft command" and still leaves the disagreeing brief unchanged. A hand-authored file with no "ingested from" text is skipped, so the command can report a clean repair while `scope:activate` still refuses. A command that copies the stored binding onto `plan.id` changes the brief's identity. That binding is file content, not a new REST read. Copying it onto an id `findParentsByPlanId` already records collides with the other brief. Minting a replacement from issue text would take identity from untrusted issue content.
Disposition: Before bind, name the command and the write. The disagree case must not delegate to `repairNonterminalIssuePlanIds`. State which field wins. Refuse when the resulting `plan.id` already occupies another artifact. Do not mint that id from issue-body text.

## No writer emits the disagreeing pair
footnote
Evidence: `git grep` for `plan.id =` under `packages/core/src` and `packages/cli/src` at this SHA finds a production write only in `attachPlanIdMint`. Ingest, admission's missing-id path, and repair's missing-id path all use that helper, which sets both fields to one mint id.
Failure mode: None for the bind. A search for a product writer of `plan.id` not equal to the stored mint will not find one in this tree.
Disposition: No new mint writer. The split is a later edit of one of the two fields. The verify gap and the hint still stand.

Road not taken: call `evaluateIssuePlanIdAdmission` from `verifyXbrief`, and replace the hint with a thin deft wrapper of `repairNonterminalIssuePlanIds`. That is the literal target. It fails for the two reasons above. It would flip if verify were redefined as lifecycle admission and the command specified which field it writes, under the existing duplicate check, with no mint from issue text.

The stored-mint defect survives. `xbrief:verify` accepts a brief whose `plan.id` disagrees with a stored `x-directive/plan-id` mint, and `scope:activate` rejects that brief with a hint that names `repairNonterminalIssuePlanIds`. The two remedy clauses survive only in the form stated in the dispositions above.

## In plain English

A hand-written brief can pass verification and then die on activate, because its plan id does not match the mint stored in the same file. The message tells the person to call an internal function, so the only way through is a hand edit.

Verification will reject that mismatch by reading the stored mint, and it will not take on activate's other work. The refusal will name a command that copies the stored mint onto the plan id when no other brief already has that id. The command will not call the internal repair helper, and it will not invent an id from the issue text.

Confirming this map means the list below is the build contract. The issue body's three suggested fixes are not. The same parent wrote the Stop 1 warrant and this map. The critic comment is the check on the findings. Whether the list covers the two pains stays open until a later critic targets those cites.

**Lean:** the refutation target survives only in the form in comment 5800361223. Verify shares the read-only stored-mint conflict and does not call activate's admission function. The refusal names a command that writes the stored binding onto plan.id, refuses a collision, and does not call the repair helper. This map is the bind.

## The read-only conflict check covers the false accept
footnote
Evidence: `git show cae371d0161bb7c03df0ab9fc312c477f7c524cc:packages/core/src/xbrief/verify.ts` returns exit 0 after schema, markdown sections, and json/md id equality. It never reads `x-directive/plan-id`. In `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts`, `bindingIdentityConflict` returns `plan.id ${planId} disagrees with stored mint ${binding.id}` when plan.id is present and unequal to the stored binding id. `evaluateIssuePlanIdAdmission` turns that string into a refusal. `packages/core/src/vbrief-activate/activate.ts` and `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts` both surface that refusal on activate. A hand-authored brief still hits that comparison: `resolveIngestProvenanceOwner` returns not-ingest-owner unless Origin or description matches `/ingested from/i`, and the id comparison runs before the owner-only origin clause.
Failure mode: None on this cite. The first harvested clause makes verify run that same read-only predicate, including the later clauses, and it does not call `evaluateIssuePlanIdAdmission`, mint, or scan siblings. Verify then rejects the brief activate already rejects.
Disposition: The harvested list stays. No added clause.

## The named command covers the hand edit
footnote
Evidence: `PLAN_ID_REPAIR_HINT` names `repairNonterminalIssuePlanIds({ vbriefDir, dryRun: true })` and then `dryRun: false`. `admissionFail` appends that hint to every identity refusal. `git grep` at this SHA finds the symbol only in `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts` and `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.test.ts`. On any `bindingIdentityConflict` the repair records action refuse and, when any row refuses, returns without writing. It also skips not-ingest-owner, so a hand-authored brief never reaches a write.
Failure mode: None on this cite. A wrapper of that function would still leave the disagreeing brief unchanged. The second harvested clause names a deft command on the disagree refusal, sets plan.id to the stored binding id, refuses a collision, and does not call the helper. That is the hand edit of plan.id.
Disposition: The harvested list stays. Other admission codes still append the same hint. Those codes are not the hand edit of plan.id. The pain's refusal is the disagree refusal. No added clause.

## The stored binding id is the field that clears the disagree
footnote
Evidence: The disagree return is the first clause of `bindingIdentityConflict`, and the message names `binding.id` as the stored mint. `mintIssuePlanId` sets a REST id to `github.issue.${restId}` with source `github-rest-id`. For that source the predicate then requires `binding.id === github.issue.${githubIssueId}` and returns. `attachPlanIdMint` assigns that same id to plan.id and to the binding. Setting plan.id to binding.id clears the first clause and leaves the REST self-check true when the binding was minted that way. Setting the binding id to a hand-authored plan.id makes the REST self-check fail, because the expected id stays `github.issue.${githubIssueId}`. A consistent fallback binding has the same direction: its id must stay equal to `mintIssuePlanId` for that origin (`github.issue.fallback...`). The fixture `refuses matching plan.id when stored binding origin/source/github_issue_id/version conflict` keeps admission conflicting when the two ids match but the REST id does not. `github.issue.<digits>` matches `PLAN_ID_FORMAT`. The collision refuse is the `findParentsByPlanId` census already in `evaluateIssuePlanIdAdmission`, excluding the file itself.
Failure mode: None on this cite. Copying the other field, or minting from issue text, leaves activate refusing. An origin mismatch or an internally inconsistent binding still refuses after the ids match. That is outside the pain's inequality against a stored `github.issue.<id>` mint, and the first harvested clause already reports those clauses from verify. The command does not claim to repair them.
Disposition: The substantiation holds. The harvested write stays plan.id set to the stored binding id. No added clause.

## The write stays inside the admission trust boundary
footnote
Evidence: The stored binding is file content. Activate already treats binding.id as the mint when the fields match, and it does not re-read GitHub. The harvested command copies that same id and refuses when `findParentsByPlanId` already records it. It does not mint from issue-body text.
Failure mode: None on this cite. A hand-authored binding can name an unused `github.issue.<id>`. That is the trust activate already grants once the fields match. The collision census is the deterministic control. Overwriting plan.id is the same mutation as the hand edit that unblocked activate, including any depends_on string that named the old id.
Disposition: No harvested control to add.

Road not taken: make plan.id win by copying it onto the binding, or mint a fresh id at promote. The first fails the REST self-check whenever the hand-authored id is not already `github.issue.<github_issue_id>`. The second takes identity from issue text, which the harvested list excludes.
What would flip the field: a well-formed REST binding whose self-check accepted an arbitrary plan.id, or an activate comparison whose stored mint was not binding.id. Neither is in this tree.

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

BLOCKER. On a greenfield first story, `xbrief:verify` passed a hand-authored brief that `scope:activate` later rejected because `plan.id` did not equal the stored mint `github.issue.<id>`. The activation remediation named an internal function — `repairNonterminalIssuePlanIds({ vbriefDir, dryRun: true })` — not a runnable `deft` command. The operator had to edit `plan.id` by hand before work could continue.

## Source

Doug first-run feedback on greenfield project **superchecker**, `@deftai/directive@0.119.6`, Claude Code host, 2026-09-22. Friction points 7 and 8.

## Expected

1. `xbrief:verify` and `scope:activate` agree on what a valid brief is (identity checks run inside verify).
2. `scope:promote` mints `plan.id` for issue-backed briefs so hand-authored or accept-drafted scopes activate cleanly.
3. Every refusal remediation is a runnable `deft …` command a consumer can copy-paste.

## Actual

- `xbrief:verify` passed the hand-written brief (false confidence).
- `scope:activate` refused: `plan.id` ≠ stored mint `github.issue.<id>`.
- Remediation text named `repairNonterminalIssuePlanIds({ vbriefDir, dryRun: true })` (engine-internal; see `PLAN_ID_REPAIR_HINT` in `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts`).
- Unblocked only by hand-editing `plan.id`.

## Environment

- Directive: `0.119.6`
- Host: Claude Code
- Flow: hand-written brief → promote → feature branch → `session:start` → `scope:activate`
- Cost: **blocked** until `plan.id` edited by hand

## Related

- Closed #4119 — `issue:ingest` omits stable `plan.id` (fixed mint at ingest). This report is the leftover consumer path: hand-authored / promote path still diverges, verify does not catch it, and recovery still names the internal repair helper.

## Adoption impact

### Affected consumer flow and version

Greenfield first-story activate on `@deftai/directive@0.119.6` after a hand-authored (or non-ingest-minted) issue-backed brief.

### Documented alternatives attempted

Remediation offered only the internal `repairNonterminalIssuePlanIds(...)` call. No `deft` verb was named. Hand-editing `plan.id` was the only path that unblocked activate.

### Observed recovery cost

Activate hard-stopped the session mid first-story; work resumed only after a manual JSON edit of `plan.id`.

### Triage owner and date

polfer / 2026-09-23 — applying `adoption-blocker` after body-evidence test from Doug first-run report.

## Suggested fix

1. Run the same identity checks inside `xbrief:verify` that activate uses.
2. Have `scope:promote` mint `plan.id` for issue-backed briefs.
3. Replace `PLAN_ID_REPAIR_HINT` with a runnable `deft …` recovery command (or make activate auto-repair with an explicit printed action).
